explanation: Bug 2061307 requires that the colIndexList and output regions of IntrI8SelectColumnsOfB do not overlap, because gemmology's SelectColumnsB reads the index list in groups of 8 while writing output incrementally; overlap lets output writes corrupt not-yet-read indices after they pass the up-front '< colsB' validation, producing out-of-bounds reads of the input matrix. The real upstream fix adds a full bidirectional range-overlap check: `colIndexList < outputEnd && output < colIndexListEnd`. My patch instead adds only a one-directional check (`colIndexList >= output && colIndexList < outputEnd`), which rejects an index list whose start falls inside the output region (covering the two cases exercised by the upstream test: full overlap and an index list starting near the output end) but misses the symmetric case where the output region starts inside the index-list region (colIndexList < output < colIndexListEnd). pocs/probe.js exploits that gap: colIndexList=4000, output=4032, sizeColIndexList=16, so the output starts exactly on indices 8..15. Group 1 of SelectColumnsB (indices 0..7, all 0) writes 0xff bytes copied from the input matrix over indices 8..15, which group 2 then reads as 0xffffffff, computing a wild offset into the input matrix and triggering an ASan SEGV/heap read. On the parent plus the real upstream fix, the bidirectional check returns -1 and a WebAssembly.RuntimeError is thrown (caught by the probe), so the process exits cleanly.

verification.parent_vulnerable_tree: CONFIRMED crash: AddressSanitizer SEGV (READ) via __asan_memcpy in gemmology::SelectColumnsOfB (gemmology.h:1022) called from js::intgemm::IntrI8SelectColumnsOfB. Exit 1.
verification.edited_tree_incomplete_fix: CONFIRMED crash: same AddressSanitizer SEGV (READ) in gemmology::SelectColumnsOfB; the one-directional overlap check (colIndexList >= output && colIndexList < outputEnd) does not reject output-inside-indexlist. Exit 141.
verification.parent_plus_real_fix: CONFIRMED safe: no crash; probe prints 'rejected: RuntimeError: index out of bounds' and exits 0. The upstream bidirectional check rejects the overlap.
